cf.title: BUG #19689: MERGE INSERT accepts a set-returning function during PREPARE but fails at EXECUTE

input.subject: BUG #19689: MERGE INSERT accepts a set-returning function during PREPARE but fails at EXECUTE

verdict_reasoning: The goal is not in question: the statement fails on every execution today, and the patch moves the error to parse analysis. The only surviving objection, maintenance-fit-1, is a fixable design point about where the check lives. A committer who knows parse analysis should decide between the p_hasTargetSRFs check and an expression kind that check_srf_call_placement() rejects, and should decide on back-patching.

brief.title: Reject set-returning functions in MERGE insert actions at parse analysis
brief.problem: A set-returning function in the VALUES of a MERGE WHEN NOT MATCHED INSERT action passes parse analysis, so PREPARE succeeds. Every EXECUTE then fails with "set-valued function called in context that cannot accept a set". The reporter saw this on 20devel, 18.6 and 17.11, and wants the error raised when the statement is analyzed.
brief.proposed_design: MERGE INSERT values are transformed with EXPR_KIND_VALUES_SINGLE, which allows SRFs and sets p_hasTargetSRFs, but transformMergeStmt() later clears hasTargetSRFs and no ProjectSet node expands the action target list. The patch checks pstate->p_hasTargetSRFs right after the INSERT values are transformed and raises an error. The check sits only in the CMD_INSERT case, so UPDATE actions and SRFs in the MERGE source do not change.
user_visible_surface: merge ... when not matched then insert values (...) containing a set-returning function now fails at parse analysis, and so at PREPARE, instead of at execution.
author_claims: The executor can never run an SRF in a MERGE INSERT action, so the statement always fails today.
The check does not affect other MERGE actions or SRFs used in the MERGE data source.
A MERGE INSERT action is meant to insert one row per candidate change row.
brief.thread_state: The bug report and one reply from the patch author with a first patch are visible. The author asks whether rejecting SRFs here is the intended behavior and has not added a regression test yet.
unclear: The material does not give the new error message text or SQLSTATE.
The proposal does not say whether MERGE UPDATE SET actions accept SRFs today and fail the same way.
The proposal does not say whether the fix should be back-patched to 17 and 18.
The proposal does not say whether a non-prepared MERGE now fails with a different error message than before.
search_queries: set-valued function cannot accept a set

objections.title: Ad hoc flag check instead of the expression-kind mechanism for SRF placement
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a MERGE action or moves MERGE UPDATE SET to a new transform path. It does not copy the p_hasTargetSRFs check, and nothing fails at build or test time. Users find out when PREPARE succeeds again and every EXECUTE fails.
objections.argument: Postgres already decides where SRFs are allowed through ParseExprKind and check_srf_call_placement(), which gives one error text per context. The patch keeps EXPR_KIND_VALUES_SINGLE, which allows SRFs, and adds a separate test in the CMD_INSERT case only (message #2). The proposal does not say whether MERGE UPDATE SET has the same gap, so the fix may cover one of two places. A committer would likely ask for a MERGE-specific expression kind, or a reason why the existing mechanism does not fit.
objections.author_must_show: Why is a p_hasTargetSRFs check in CMD_INSERT better than giving MERGE action expressions their own expression kind, and does MERGE UPDATE SET need the same fix?

critic.reasoning: check_srf_call_placement() is the existing place for this rule, and the proposal gives no reason for a separate flag test. The MERGE UPDATE SET part should be dropped: EXPR_KIND_UPDATE_SOURCE already rejects SRFs at parse analysis, as far as I recall.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: The patch changes which expressions parse analysis accepts in the values of a MERGE insert action.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: Message #1 reproduces the bug on 17.11 and 18.6, and the proposal does not say whether to back-patch.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The check is a separate p_hasTargetSRFs test in the CMD_INSERT case of parse_merge.c, outside check_srf_call_placement().

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Why is a p_hasTargetSRFs check in the CMD_INSERT case better than giving MERGE insert values an expression kind that check_srf_call_placement() rejects?
Should the fix be back-patched to 17 and 18, where message #1 also reproduces the failure?
What are the new error message text and SQLSTATE, and do they match what check_srf_call_placement() reports for other contexts?
Does a non-prepared MERGE with such a function now report a different error message than before?
Do MERGE UPDATE SET actions already reject set-returning functions at parse analysis?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows parse analysis and the MERGE transform code would have to own it. No committer has spoken in the two visible messages.
committability.liability: One parse-analysis check in parse_merge.c and its error message, plus the back-patch decision for 17 and 18. If the check stays a separate flag test, later MERGE action paths must remember to copy it.
committability.author_follow_up: The author offers in message #2 to add a regression test in the next version once the intended behavior is confirmed.

priority.reason: The patch is 1.9 KB in one parser file and fixes a reported bug that makes a prepared MERGE fail on every execution. Few users write a set-returning function in MERGE insert values, and the remaining design point is small.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the error text, the SQLSTATE and the exact placement of the check are unverified. The material also does not show whether a stored SQL-function body that holds such a MERGE can exist and would fail to restore.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert MERGE patch
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert MERGE patch
Reverted commit(s): MERGE SQL Command following SQL:2016; New files for MERGE; Improve parse representation for MERGE; MERGE syntax diagram correction; Allow cpluspluscheck to pass by renaming variable
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commits d204ef63776b8a00ca220adec23979091564e465,
83454e3c2b28141c0db01c7d2027e01040df5249 and a few more commits thereafter
(complete list at the end) related to MERGE feature.

While the feature was fully functional, with sufficient test coverage and
necessary documentation, it was felt that some parts of the executor and
parse-analyzer can use a different design and it wasn't possible to do that in
the available time. So it was decided to revert the patch for PG11 and retry
again in the future.

Thanks again to all reviewers and bug reporters.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add tests for PL/pgSQL SRFs
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds regression tests for PL/pgSQL set-returning functions, covering the case where materialize mode is required but no result TupleDesc exists, and other `SETOF RECORD` versus `TABLE (...)` calls. The author also suggested replacing the confusing "materialize mode required" error for the missing-TupleDesc case with the column definition list error.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said the tests cover one unremarkable ereport(ERROR) line and are not worth core regression test cycles. He agreed the error message could be split into two conditions, but wanted different wording and a change in all ten places that throw this error, not only in plpgsql. The thread shows no new patch after his reply.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
AFAICT this test case adds coverage of exactly one line of code,
and that line is an unremarkable ereport(ERROR).  I can't get
excited about spending test cycles on this forevermore, especially
not core-regression-test cycles.

precedents_retrieved.title: copy_srf (was COPY as a set returning function)
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a core set-returning function copy_srf() that reads a file or program output with the COPY FROM machinery and returns the rows to a query, so users can select or filter them without a temp table or a file_fdw table. Later versions added a TupleDesc parameter to BeginCopy() and BeginCopyFrom() so COPY can run without a relation in pg_class.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier closed it as immature because the new rsTupDesc parameter overlaps with the relation that callers already pass to BeginCopyFrom(), and because the function used NextCopyFromRawFields and skipped the checks in NextCopyFrom(). The author had not chosen between a function, a RETURNING clause on COPY, or an extension hook, and reviewers asked for tests and documentation. Copy from STDIN also failed with a protocol error.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Looking at the last patch proposed, I find the current patch proposed
as immature, as rsTupDesc basically overlaps with the relation a
caller can define in BeginCopyFrom(), so marking this patch as
"returned with feedback".

precedents_retrieved.title: Reimplement targetlist SRFs using ROWS FROM ()
precedents_retrieved.summary: Andres Freund proposed removing set-returning functions in the target list (tSRFs) from generic expression evaluation by rewriting them in the planner into ROWS FROM () function RTEs joined laterally. The patch series also dropped the least-common-multiple row count rule, removed materialization from nodeFunctionscan.c, added syntax for returning a record unexpanded, and forbade SRFs in UPDATE, ORDER BY and GROUP BY.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the LATERAL rewrite added about 500 lines of hard-to-read planner code and could lock in incompatibilities. He drafted a planner prototype that evaluates tSRFs in a Result-like pipeline node, and both authors agreed to continue that way. He also objected that skipping materialization gives wrong results on rescan, for example inside a nestloop, and that forbidding SRFs in ORDER BY was arbitrary. Michael Paquier then returned the entry with feedback because of low activity.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: But it's now looking to me like the latter would be a lot simpler from the point of view of planner complexity, and in particular from the point of view of proving correctness (equivalence of the query transformation).

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow pageinspect's bt_page_stats function to return a set of rows instead of a single row
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch first changed pageinspect's bt_page_stats to return a set of rows covering a range of B-Tree pages, with a pageinspect version bump to 1.11. After review it added a separate function, bt_multi_page_stats, which takes an index, a starting block number and a block count.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane listed open issues before the patch could be committed: no documentation update, no simple way to ask for all remaining pages (a count one too large raises an error), and a regression test that depends on tuple layout. He then showed the test fails on a 32-bit machine. The author did not address this feedback, and Michael Paquier marked the entry Returned with feedback after four weeks of inactivity.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This feedback has not been addressed and the thread is idle four
weeks, so I have marked this CF entry as RwF.

precedents_retrieved.title: introduce optimized linear search functions that return index of matching element
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds SIMD linear search functions, pg_lfind8_idx() and pg_lfind8_ge_idx(), that return the index of the first matching byte instead of true/false. It came from the radix tree work for lazy vacuum dead tuple storage, and this version also reworks the simd.h helpers it uses.
precedents_retrieved.objection: John Naylor judged that this level of abstraction is not right for the intended use case, the radix tree for lazy vacuum. He said some of the low-level simd.h improvements would be used later in that work, and he returned the entry with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
As I mentioned in the radix tree thread, I don't believe this level of
abstraction is appropriate for the intended use case.

precedents_retrieved.title: Range Merge Join
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend the existing Merge Join executor node to also handle range conditions (containment @> / <@ between a range and an element, or scalar BETWEEN-AND / paired inequalities), optionally combined with equality conditions, by adding a range_cond alongside the merge_cond and extending the merge join state machine. The planner would detect such conditions and use estimates to choose this "Range Merge Join" over other strategies.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tomas Vondra's review found that the patch still did not compile with asserts, had no regression tests exercising the new code, and lacked comments explaining the new functions and the reworked executor blocks. Two months later Julien Rouhaud asked whether the author planned to continue; no response from the author is visible before the entry was returned with feedback. Earlier, Jeff Davis had raised concerns about multiple join keys and suggested a CustomScan extension, which the authors declined.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I took a brief look at the patch, and I think there are two main issues
preventing it from moving forward.

precedents_retrieved.title: bytea PL/Perl transform
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Eisentraut, Alexander Korotkov, Tom Lane
precedents_retrieved.summary: A new contrib extension adds a PL/Perl transform for bytea, so bytea values reach Perl as native byte strings instead of hexadecimal text. The goal is to save memory and time and make bytea easier to use in PL/Perl.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch put a transform for a built-in type in a separate extension, while reviewers wanted it inside plperl itself, as part of a "plperl[u] 1.1" upgrade. Tom Lane moved the entry back to Waiting on Author and also found the documentation inadequate, since it does not define "native Perl octet strings" and has no real example. The visible messages show no revised patch before the entry was returned.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The last version of the patch still provides transform for builtin
type in a separate extension.  As discussed upthread such transforms
don't need separate extensions, and could be provided as part of
upgrades of existing extensions.

precedents_retrieved.title: Permute underscore separated components of columns before fuzzy matching
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend the fuzzy column-name matching behind the "Perhaps you meant" hint so that it also checks permutations of up to three underscore-separated words. A swap of two words costs the same as one mistyped character, and the permutation is skipped when the typed name has more than six underscores.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the patch adds opaque, almost undocumented code to the matching function, and he doubted that many users want this behavior. He also noted that adjacent underscores and leading or trailing underscores are not handled well. The visible messages show no reply from the author after this review, and the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
However, we *do*
need to be concerned about its maintainability, and I think the patch
falls down badly there: it adds a chunk of very opaque and essentially
undocumented code, that people will need to reverse-engineer anytime
they are studying this function.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Reject concurrent sequence refreshes".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Reject concurrent sequence refreshes".
Reverted commit(s): Reject concurrent sequence refreshes.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit f38afa4abb04e85530c94b88daf11c089375daca.

That commit fixed a race that could leave stale sequence values on the
subscriber after 'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'. It did so by
raising an ERROR during 'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'
whenever a sequence synchronization worker was already running for the
subscription.

That approach caused intermittent buildfarm failures, because the existing
tests did not ensure the sequencesync worker had stopped before executing
'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'. While discussing how to fix
the tests, we concluded that blocking the command while a sequencesync
worker is running is inconvenient for users. So we will fix the original
race differently in a follow-up commit.

roaster_notes.note: The only precedent, [P4], is about reimplementing target-list SRFs in the planner, a different idea. Its recorded reason (planner complexity, rescan correctness) does not apply to a parse-time check in MERGE INSERT. The thread cites no earlier discussion of this idea, so no precedent was found.

From the standards and compatibility angle, the change only moves an error that always happens at executor start to parse analysis. No working query, script or dump changes behaviour, and the SQL standard has no set-returning functions in MERGE insert values. Not checked without the code: the new error text and SQLSTATE, whether a stored SQL-function body holding such a MERGE could fail restore, and whether a back-patch is intended.

The patch adds one parse-analysis check in parse_merge.c, with no change to on-disk format, WAL, catalogs, wire protocol or extension ABI. One edge was not checked: if a stored SQL function body holding such a MERGE can be created, its dump would fail to restore during pg_upgrade.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. It moves an existing error for SRFs in MERGE INSERT values from execution to parse analysis, so it adds no new capability, default, privilege check, information path or resource use for any role.

The fix is small, touches only parse_merge.c, and costs nothing for users who do not use the feature. The only objection from this angle is about where the check lives. Back-patch scope and the error text could not be checked from the material.

This is a bug fix that moves an existing, always-failing case to an earlier error at parse analysis. No existing feature, extension or hook does this, and the fix adds no new mechanism. [P4] is about how target-list SRFs are run in general, so its reasons do not apply here.

This is a bug fix. The statement already fails on every execution, so moving the error to parse analysis takes nothing from working users and adds no feature surface. A field report in message #1 reproduces it on 17.11, 18.6 and 20devel. Demand is not the question here; whether to back-patch it is.
